name: Merab Dvalishvili
summary: Former bantamweight champion (21-5) and the division's most relentless wrestler: three title defences in 2025 before Petr Yan took the belt on a unanimous decision in December. Wins by sheer volume of takedown attempts and pace over 15 or 25 minutes.

how_they_fight.Striking: Busy but light: about 4.8 significant strikes a minute at 46%, used to cover level changes. Only three KO/TKO wins (verified), last one Marlon Moraes R2 in 2021. Out-landed Yan on volume in the rematch, but Yan's shots did more damage (POST Wrestling).
how_they_fight.Grappling: Elite chain wrestler: about 3.9 takedowns per 15 at 40%, i.e. huge attempt volume. Shoots, gets stuffed, backs out and re-shoots (Cageside on O'Malley 2). Submitted O'Malley with a modified D'Arce/guillotine at 4:42 of R3. Yan stuffed more than two dozen attempts in December.
how_they_fight.Defense: Durable: stopped once in 26 fights (Ricky Simon, submission at 5:00 of R3, 2018). Absorbs only about 2.1 strikes a minute. Nose broken repeatedly; he said in April it was broken in two places and he is deferring reconstruction until retirement (LowKick MMA).
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: The pace is the weapon: gets stronger as opponents tire, and 16 of 21 wins are decisions. Finishes (verified): R1 x1, R2 x2, R3 x2, so he almost never finishes early; his only UFC title-fight finish came late in R3 (O'Malley). Losses are all decisions except the Simon sub. Lost the Yan rematch on the cards (49-46, 49-47, 48-47 per POST Wrestling) when the takedowns dried up.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Single-minded game plan, high work rate, strong in scrambles. When the shot isn't working he keeps shooting rather than switching approach, which is how Yan beat him.

patterns: Takedown volume from the opening bell; re-shoots after every stuff
Wins late rounds by out-pacing tired opponents
Most wins on the scorecards; finishes, when they come, are R2-R3
Very hard to stop; has never been KO'd
concerns: Yan's takedown defence neutralised him in the rematch; no clear plan B on the feet
Low-power striking lets counter-punchers land the heavier shots
Repeatedly broken nose; Yan says he will target it
Lost a freestyle wrestling rematch to Henry Cejudo by pin in 36 seconds at RAF 12 in August (after beating him 11-8 at RAF Georgia in July), per EssentiallySports
keys_to_beat: Stuff the first shots and punish the re-shot with knees and uppercuts
Attack the body to blunt his pace
Win the exchanges with heavier strikes; don't get drawn into a scramble-fest

news.text: Coach John Wood says this is 'a different Merab' after strong sparring and conditioning; he is motivated to reclaim the title.
Lost an RAF 12 freestyle wrestling rematch to Henry Cejudo by pinfall in 36 seconds; he had won their first RAF match 11-8 in Tbilisi on July 11.
Broke his nose again in sparring (a knee); deferring reconstruction until after retirement.
Opened a +140 underdog to Yan at DraftKings.
